Vanessa / team — attaching a redline (MedTab_DPA_Redline.pdf) and a short plain-text suggestion for one-liner contract language (suggested_model_clause.txt). Key points: 

- "Model-update opt-out" language: we offer a contract clause where customer data is excluded from any model training or improvement. We prefer to couple that with an operational guarantee (ephemeral session retention of <= 72 hours by default, logs-only retention for troubleshooting) and an audit trail showing no retention beyond that window.

- Ownership language: we can put a section that explicitly states tenant inputs and generated outputs are treated as Customer Data and that Redwood will not assert ownership or licensing claims over those outputs for the purposes of model training or resale. That should satisfy your export/custody ask.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a roster and can provide an onshore-only export lane for US-hosted customers where exports are staged to an onshore KMS and SFTP endpoint. Note: onshore/export lane requests may add a small ops lead time for enrollment and SLA commitments.

Attachments in this thread: MedTab_DPA_Redline.pdf (redline of DPA with two clause options), suggested_model_clause.txt (exact language we propose for the DPA addendum).

I called out two practical tradeoffs in the redline: (1) evidence vs. absolute technical restriction — absolute removal of any logging may impede debugging; we suggest a minimal troubleshooting log retention (28 days) but with strict access controls and immediate deletion upon request in pilot scope, which most customers accept. (2) Subprocessor gating — we can commit to an onshore export lane but need a 2-week lead time for operational onboarding.

Let me know if MedTab wants the stricter "no-logging" route and we'll price the ops lockbox/scoped gateway as an add-on.

Kimberly Park
